title: Unified Attention Kernel Signature Registry and Calibration
creator: Priya Singh
description: Create a unified registry that records model/layer kernel compatibility signatures and a calibration harness that computes stability scores for attention kernel choices (FlashAttention v2 vs v3 and internal fallbacks). The registry will power deterministic kernel-routing decisions and regression detection during rollouts; the calibration harness will generate per-model thresholds used by the runtime to avoid oscillation and spike regressions during prefill and decode phases.
acceptance_criteria: Signature registry persists per-model, per-layer compatibility metadata and last-known-good kernel mapping
Calibration harness produces a stability score and recommended threshold values for at least 10 representative models (small->large) and two sequence-length profiles
Runtime can consume the registry to deterministically route kernels in canary mode for a single tenant without operator restart
Automated regression alert triggers when stability score drops by >15% vs baseline during a rolling canary
Integration tests in CI validate that a mismatched signature causes a safe fallback behavior (no crash, logged telemetry, degraded but functional latency)
reproducer_steps: 2) Deploy the registry service locally (docker-compose) and load sample signatures from tools/fixtures/signatures.json
3) Run calibration harness: tools/calibrate --model gpt-small --seq 2048 --profiles fast,balanced
4) Start runtime in canary mode: RUNTIME_CANARY=eng-246801 ./bin/runtime --registry=http://localhost:8080
5) Replay saved traffic profile monitor/fixtures/seq2048-replay.json and observe kernel routing and stability metrics in /metrics
6) Intentionally swap a signature entry to force incorrectly chosen kernel and confirm fallback to CPU-safe path and alerting
perf_baseline: Baseline measured on a mixed-tenant cluster: p50 decode latency 23ms, p95 79ms for gpt-medium@seq1024 using FlashAttention-v2 compiled kernels. Calibration should not regress p95 >10% versus baseline for targets in 'balanced' profile.
decisions: Use a lightweight signature composed of: (model_arch_hash, layer_dim, kv_cache_layout, quant_profile) to avoid storing full binary fingerprints
Store suggested kernel preference and an empirically-derived stability_score in registry entries
Calibration runs will be scheduled as an asynchronous CI job and as an on-demand cluster job for private deployments
Runtime will treat registry entries as advisory in default mode; in 'pinning' release mode the registry becomes authoritative and will force-fallback if mismatch detected
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + local end-to-end harness (this ticket)
Phase 1 (lab): calibration on C4 cluster across 10 models, capture stability baselines and thresholds
Phase 2 (canary): enable registry advisory routing for 2% traffic of internal test tenant; monitor stability and errors for 72h
Phase 3 (gradual): expand advisory routing to 25% then 50% if no regressions; if stable, promote to pinning mode for non-critical tenants
Rollback: automatic reversion to last-known-good kernel mapping if stability_score drops >15% or error rate increases by 5x
risks: Inaccurate signatures could cause silent performance regressions if runtime treats registry as authoritative
Calibration noise: small benchmark suites may not capture tail-case inputs leading to oscillation in routing
Operational overhead: storing and syncing registry across private deployments will need encryption and migration support
Edge-models (exotic dims/quant) may not have precomputed calibration and will fall back to safer slow paths increasing cost
dependencies: infra/registry-storage (SRE changes to allow low-latency lookups)
